name: Obligation of Aliyah laRegel (Appearance at the Temple)
notes: Who is obligated to appear at the Temple on pilgrimage festivals, exemptions for deaf-mutes, minors, women, lame, blind, sick, etc. Details of minimum age for minors (Beit Shammai vs. Beit Hillel).

name: Olat Reiyah (Burnt-Offering of Appearance)
notes: The burnt-offering brought upon appearing at the Temple during the three pilgrimage festivals; minimum value requirements and disputes between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel.

name: Simchat Yom Tov (Rejoicing on the Festival)
notes: Obligation to rejoice on pilgrimage festivals through peace-offerings; how priests and Israelites fulfill the obligation of rejoicing differently; what foods qualify for simcha.

name: Shalmei Simcha (Peace-Offerings of Rejoicing)
notes: Festival peace-offerings brought specifically to fulfill the obligation of rejoicing on Yom Tov; minimum values, sources of funding (non-sacred vs. second tithe), and timing.

name: Tashlumin (Make-Up Days for Festival Offering)
notes: If one failed to bring the Festival peace-offering on the first day, he may make it up throughout the remaining days of the festival. After the festival passes, no restitution is owed.

name: Semichah on Offerings on Yom Tov (Laying Hands on Festival Day)
notes: The dispute among the Zugot pairs (five pairs) over whether one may lay hands on an offering on a Festival day; relates to labor prohibitions on Yom Tov.

name: Am HaAretz and Ritual Purity
notes: The status of an am haaretz with respect to ritual purity; their garments as sources of impurity for those more scrupulous; trusted periods (winepress season, pilgrimage festival).

name: Perushim (Those Scrupulous in Purity)
notes: The class of people who are meticulously careful in ritual purity; their garments are considered impure with the treading of a zav for priests eating teruma.

name: Tumat Midras (Impurity by Treading/Pressure)
notes: Impurity conveyed when a zav or niddah treads on or sits/lies upon an object; the garments of an am haaretz are considered midras for perushim, and so on up the levels of purity.

name: Levels of Purity (Non-Sacred, Tithes, Teruma, Kodesh, Mei Chatat)
hebrew: מדרגות הטהרה: חולין, מעשר, תרומה, קודש, חטאת
notes: The graduated system of purity levels: one who immersed for non-sacred food may not eat tithes; for tithes may not eat teruma; for teruma may not eat sacrificial food; for sacrificial food may not touch purification waters. Each level has stricter requirements.

name: Stringencies of Kodesh over Terumah (Greater Strictness for Sacrificial Food)
notes: Detailed halakhic differences requiring greater purity for sacrificial foods than for teruma: immersing vessels inside other vessels, carrying trodden objects, hands, fourth-degree impurity, etc.

name: Tevul Yom and Purity Levels
notes: The distinction in purity requirements for a tevul yom (one who immersed that day) regarding teruma vs. kodesh; immersion without intent to achieve purity status is ineffective.

name: Onen's Prohibition from Sacrificial Food
notes: An acute mourner (onen) on the day of bereavement requires immersion to eat sacrificial food, but not for teruma; similarly one who is mechusar kapparah.

name: Trustworthiness of Amei HaAretz in Purity (Ne'emanut)
notes: Periods and circumstances under which amei haaretz are deemed trustworthy regarding ritual purity: during winepress season, during pilgrimage festivals, within Modi'im boundaries, etc.

name: Purification of Temple Vessels After the Festival
notes: After the pilgrimage festival when amei haaretz entered the Temple, all vessels required immersion. Disputes about when this is done; golden and bronze altars are exempt as they are like the ground.

name: Prohibition of Expounding Arayot Before Three
notes: The prohibition of publicly expounding the laws of forbidden sexual relations before three or more people; classified with other restricted topics of Torah study.

name: Restriction on Teaching Maaseh Bereishit (Cosmogony)
notes: The restriction against expounding the account of Creation before two or more individuals; paired with the restriction on Maaseh Merkavah.

name: Restriction on Teaching Maaseh Merkavah (Divine Chariot)
notes: The prohibition of teaching the Design of the Divine Chariot even one-on-one, unless the student is wise and understands on his own; source for esoteric teaching restrictions.

name: Four Forbidden Speculative Topics (Above, Below, Before, After)
notes: The four matters one should not speculate about: what is above the firmament, what is below the earth, what was before creation, what will be after the world ends.

name: Dissolution of Vows — Lack of Biblical Basis
notes: The mishna's statement that the halakhot of dissolving vows 'fly in the air' with no scriptural support; categorization of Torah topics by the strength of their biblical basis.

name: Mountains Hanging by a Hair (Minimal Biblical Basis for Major Topics)
notes: The category of halakhot — Shabbat, Festival peace-offerings, meilah — that have minimal written basis in the Torah yet have elaborate rabbinic detail; methodological classification of Torah topics.

name: The Five Pairs (Zugot)
notes: The five pairs of leading sages who served as Nasi and Av Beit Din in the Second Temple period; their disputes over semichah on festival offerings are recorded in Mishnah Chagigah.

name: Fourth-Degree Impurity (Revi'i l'Tumah)
notes: The concept that sacrificial food can be rendered impure to a fourth degree (disqualified but not transmitting impurity further), while teruma is only susceptible to third-degree impurity; a unique stringency for kodesh.

name: Haver vs. Am HaAretz Distinction
notes: The social/religious distinction between a haver (one meticulous in purity and tithes) and an am haaretz; practical halakhic consequences for accepting food and vessels from an am haaretz.

name: Modi'im Boundary for Purity Trustworthiness
notes: Potters within the boundary of Modi'im (15 mil from Jerusalem) are trusted regarding purity of earthenware vessels; those outside are not; geographic demarcation for purity trustworthiness.
